title: The 10 Best Air Ratchets
subtitle: 1/4, 3/8 and 1/2-inch pneumatic ratchets for engine bays and fast fastener run-down, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An air ratchet spins nuts and bolts on and off far faster than a hand ratchet once they're broken loose, and it fits where an impact gun won't. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (70+ ft-lbs of torque, a variable-speed throttle, a 360-degree exhaust and a weight of 2.6 lbs or less). Most are 3/8-inch drive; 1/4-inch palm ratchets get under dashboards, and 1/2-inch drives suit bigger fasteners. They run from about $31 for Dynamic Power's 3/8-inch to $191 for Ingersoll Rand's 109XPA.

buyers_guide.a: An impact wrench hammers tight bolts loose; an air ratchet spins loose fasteners in and out quickly and fits in tighter spaces. Mechanics use both: break it loose with the impact or a breaker bar, run it out with the ratchet.
3/8-inch covers most engine work. 1/4-inch palm ratchets fit under dashboards and handle small fasteners. 1/2-inch suits larger bolts if you already own 1/2-inch sockets.

buyers_guide.q: How much air does an air ratchet use?
buyers_guide.a: Usually 3 to 5 CFM at 90 PSI. Ratchets run in short bursts, so a mid-size compressor keeps up easily.

buyers_guide.q: Can I break bolts loose with an air ratchet?
buyers_guide.a: Not tight ones. Most ratchets are rated 25 to 75 ft-lbs. Forcing them past that wears the head out fast. Use a breaker bar or impact wrench first.
Yes. A few drops of air tool oil in the inlet before each use keeps the motor and head working smoothly.
